title: Imprimitive heavy lines are a self-similar orbit shrink into mu_{n/gcd} sub-tower (F3<->F8 descent)
evidence: Exact integer probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/probe_C052_imprimitive_orbit_shrink.py and probe_C052_gcd_disambiguate.py compute the Vieta-pinned bad-scalar set lacBad(mu_n,a,t=d) = {e_t(S) mod q : S subset mu_n, |S|=a, e_1(S)=...=e_{t-1}(S)=0} EXACTLY over proper-subgroup primes q=1 mod n (q=1009,5009,20113; n=8,16,32; all proper dyadic subgroups, n<<q). This is precisely the object the cited file DyadicLacunaryDeltaStar.lean (lacBad / lacBad_smul_closed) governs. TWO sub-claims tested. (i) ORBIT-DIVISIBILITY n/gcd(d,n) | #nonzero-lacBad: HOLDS, zero violations across all (a,b,n,q) -- this is the already-in-tree axiom-clean fact (lacBad_smul_closed + orderOf_dvd_card_of_mul_mem). (ii)/(iii) THE CENTRAL THESIS 'imprimitive gcd(d,n)>1 => heavy (up to full q), primitive concentrate': REFUTED, exactly backwards. Heaviness is MONOTONE DECREASING in gcd(d,n): at n=16 max#lacBad by gcd(d,n)= {1:3281(~=q at q=20113), 2:41, 4:5, 8:2, 16:1}; the near-full-q heavy rows are ALL primitive ((8,7),(7,6),(9,8) with d=1, gcd(d,n)=1). Same direction under the issue's alternate 'pull-back' notion gcd(a,b,n). The primitive lines (full eigenratio order n) reach full-q incidence; imprimitive lines (small eigenratio order n/gcd) are LIGHT because the vanishing constraints e_1=...=e_{d-1}=0 collapse the variety. The orbit-divisibility law C052 invokes only forces #lacBad to be a MULTIPLE of n/gcd(d,n) -- a SMALLER multiple-constraint for larger gcd, i.e. it gives LESS forced size, the opposite of a heaviness/per-coset-multiplicity-growth mechanism. There is no self-similar orbit-shrink amplification and no F8 descent realized this way.
honest_note: What survives is the divisibility sub-fact (claim i), which is already proven axiom-clean in-tree (DyadicLacunaryDeltaStar.lean lacBad_smul_closed, MCAEigenstackOrbitLaw.lean orderOf_dvd_card_of_mul_mem); generalizing monomial_badSet_mul_invariant from gap d=1 to general d is routine (eigenratio g^d) and the probe confirms n/gcd(d,n) | #lacBad. But that is exactly the part C052 already treated as known; the NEW claim (the connection's actual content) -- that gcd>1 heaviness IS the F8 2-adic descent via a self-similar orbit shrink -- is the part that is false. NOTE: the issue grounding (scripts/probes/_issue407_full.md lines 119/218-231) itself asserts 'imprimitive gcd>1 lines are HEAVY up to full q'; that assertion is about a DIFFERENT (raw line-ball / monomial-stack) incidence with a small-n caveat, NOT the Vieta-pinned lacBad object that DyadicLacunaryDeltaStar.lean and C052 invoke; in lacBad the direction inverts, so C052's binding of the heuristic to the lacBad/eigenratio object is the specific error. Scope: tested small n=8,16,32 with multiple large proper-subgroup primes (the structural orbit/heaviness direction is q-robust per the 3-prime check); did not test prize-size n=2^30 (intractable to enumerate C(n,a), and unnecessary -- the refuted claim is structural). Recommend logging to DISPROOF_LOG.md.
